50 Cent ordered back into bankruptcy court after flashing cash on Instagram

Can someone who is legally-savvy explain to me what this would mean for him? I mean, he declares bankruptcy but has cash. So what? Shouldn't he want to avoid declaring bankruptcy? Why is it an issue for him; I don't see how he benefits from declaring bankruptcy when he really isn't bankrupt.
Getting debts forgiven means not losing the money he has.
He declared bankruptcy to avoid some large lawsuits (worth millions of dollars). So, if he still has assets that weren't mentioned, the court needs to divvy that up among his debtors.

When one declares bankruptcy, he is vowing under oath and penalty of perjury that he does not now have the means to pay off his debts and probably never will have enough means to do so. Part of this process is he literally is supposed to declare everything he has in assets. Not just cash, stocks, etc., but literally everything...house, car, clothes, silverware, dishes, you name it. Everything has to appear on his declaration page to the court.

I am not certain if 50 Cent is declaring chapter 7 bankruptcy (which means he doesn't have anything of value and huge debts) or chapter 13 (which means he has some assets that he wants to keep and he has huge debts). In either case, he was supposed to tell the court all of his assets. This is so the court can determine if there is anything that can be used to pay the creditors he owes. If he is not truthful in his asset declaration (IE he is trying to hide assets), the bankruptcy judge is going to be pissed. The judge can throw the case out, in which case 50 Cent then has to pay all his debtors in full. Imagine a vulture coming to pick the corpse clean, yeah, it's pretty much like that.

In other words, if 50 Cent is hiding assets he is an idiot and if his lawyer knew that he was hiding assets the lawyer should be facing a disciplinary hearing.

The reason somebody declares bankruptcy is to get the elephant off your back. Instead of spending the majority of your money on paying debts that you most likely will never make head way on, the court wipes the debt and you can start trying to rebuild your financial life. In most cases, people still have an income, but they just got so far over their head that they can't get out from under it. Their income is being eaten up by their debts. So you declare bankruptcy, have the debts wiped, and you can start keeping more of the income.
